text: Gold dipped to about $3,693 in Asian trade, its lowest since September 2025, then recovered to about $3,731, roughly 0.2% above Wednesday's US close.
Silver bounced about 1% to near $45.40 after an overnight low around $44.54, easing the gold/silver ratio to about 82.2.
Nasdaq futures rose about 2% and S&P 500 futures about 1.2% before the open as Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share ahead of its Nasdaq debut.
US weekly jobless claims rose to 203,000, a little above the 197,000 expected; the dollar index eased slightly afterwards but stayed near a 19-month high.
Brent crude held near $92 a barrel, little changed after settling at $91.95 on Wednesday, as supply-surplus worries offset attacks on ships near Hormuz.
Bitcoin traded near $63,700 early Thursday, about $400 below a day earlier, as ETF outflows continued.
The yen stayed just under 160 per dollar ahead of Japan's October inflation data, with Tokyo's intervention warnings still in view.
